title: MCU-NPS AI Learning Initiatives
description:
# MCU-NPS AI Learning Initiatives Hackathon

## 🚀 Event Overview & Goals
The **Joint Marine Corps University (MCU) - Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) AI Learning Initiatives Hackathon** brings together end-users, technical developers, and operational subject matter experts to harness Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to solve critical educational, administrative, and training challenges across the defense education enterprise.

Aligned with the **TECOM Campaign Plan 2025** (LOE 1D & 4B) and **Training & Education 2030**, this initiative aims to:
- **Accelerate AI Integration:** Transition data-enabled processes and AI/ML prototypes into Marine Corps and DoW training and education systems.
- **Optimize Human Performance:** Leverage AI capabilities to personalize learning, automate workflows, and improve learning and decision-making.
- **Build AI Literacy:** Build hands-on AI/ML technical literacy by bridging the gap between tactical operational requirements and technical capability development.

---

## 🛠️ What Participants Will Build
Teams will collaborate over four intensive days to build **scalable, operationally relevant software prototypes** addressing key education and training use cases:

* **Personalized Learning:** Adaptive curricula, individualized feedback systems, and tailored learning paths.
* **Simulation & Virtual Training:** Next-generation capabilities enhancing realism and effectiveness in training simulations.
* **Performance Assessment:** Objective evaluation tools for skills assessment, knowledge verification, and tactical decision-making metrics.
* **Content Generation:** Automated creation of training scenarios, curricula, exercises, and knowledge bases.
* **Operational Support:** Just-in-time learning delivery, administrative workflow automation, and data analytics.
* **Wargaming:** Tools for wargame execution, learning evaluation, and decision-making analysis.
* **High-Value User Submissions:** Select operational problem statements submitted directly by registered participants.

---

## 👥 Eligibility & Participant Roles
Participation is open to **Active Duty/Reserve Marines, Government Civilians, Sister-Service Personnel, Industry Partners, and Academic Experts**. All applicants select one of the following roles:

* **Hacker (Technical Developers):** Leads software development, model building, data engineering, and prototype construction. *(Preferred backgrounds: AI, ML, Data Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering).*
* **Subject Matter Expert (SME):** Defines problem statements, provides operational context, ensures tactical relevance, and guides solution architecture.

---

## ⭐ What Makes It Special
* **Unique Collaboration:** Combines MCU’s deep operational insights within Professional Military Education (PME) with NPS’s world-class technical leadership and Digital Transformation Accelerator (DTA).
* **Actionable Transition Pathways:** Approved use cases and high-performing prototypes receive direct visibility for transition onto authorized defense software platforms.

---

## 📅 Event Schedule (15–18 September 2026)

| Date | Activity |
|:---|:---|
| **15 Sep 2026** | **Kickoff & Team Alignment:** Opening remarks, use case familiarization, tool presentations, and team formation (MCU & NPS). |
| **16–17 Sep 2026** | **Prototype Sprint:** Intensive team-based development, programming, and model building. |
| **18 Sep 2026** | **Demonstration & Awards:** Final presentations, judging by leadership, and recognition of top teams. |

---

## 📌 Critical Dates & Administrative Information
* **Event Dates:** 15–18 September 2026
* **Application Deadline:** **14 August 2026 at 2359 EST**
* **Participant Selection Notification:** 21 August 2026
* **Security Classification:** **UNCLASSIFIED**
* **In-Person Hub Locations:** 
  * Marine Corps University / EDCOM (Quantico, VA)
  * Naval Postgraduate School (Monterey, CA)
* **Funding:** TAD/TDY travel funding is the responsibility of the participant’s parent command.
* **Awards:** Non-monetary, non-binding official recognition.

---

### Getting on Base at MCU

#### Base Access Requirements for Hackathon Attendees at Marine Corps University

All participants must ensure their ability to access MCB Quantico from 9/15 to 9/18.

For complete base access guidance, visit the [MCB Quantico Base Access Portal](https://www.quantico.marines.mil/Info/Base-Access/).

---

#### Civilian Visitor Instructions

Civilian visitors who do not possess a Common Access Card (CAC) must complete the following steps:

**Step 1:** Register in DBIDS.

**Step 2:** Print the NAVMC 5512 form.

**Step 3:** Bring the printed NAVMC 5512 form and two forms of valid ID to the MCB Quantico Visitor Control Center.

**Step 4:** Obtain a pass at the Visitor Control Center.

> **Tip:** It is recommended to arrive early to pick up your base access pass at the Visitor Control Center. Additional details can be found on the [Civilian Visitor Access Page](https://www.quantico.marines.mil/Info/Base-Access/Civilian-Non-Military/).

---

### What to bring

Bring your own device. 

At MCU, teams will use our wireless network (CampusNet) to access the internet and available tools.

At NPS, wi-fi will be available for the event.

### GenAI.mil Access at MCU

Users must have a CAC card/CAC reader to access GenAI.mil

GenAI.mil can be accessed through CampusNet for the Gemini Model only. ChatGPT and Grok must be accessed through a NIPR connection. 

A limited number of MCEN ports will be available in Lecture Hall #3 (room 3123) for users that want to use Grok or ChatGPT through GenAI.mil over NIPR.

Teams that bring a MCEN machine will be able to use CampusNet with VPN to access Grok or ChatGPT through GenAI.mil over NIPR.

### Dress

#### Civilians: Business Casual when hacking Business Professional when presenting for judges

#### MCU: UOD at MCU will be Cammies

## Registration & Entry Requirements

All Hackathon participants **MUST** be registered through the MCeLE registration form listed on MARADMIN 350/26 or confirm attendance through appropriate POC at the physical location the participant is planning to attend.


---

## Required Actions Prior to Arrival

Participants are responsible for completing the following actions prior to arrival:
- Ensure access to location instructions have been followed in accordance with MCU/MCB Quantico and NPS access guidance and policies.
- Access and participate in the event using provided account credentials in the [USMC Hackathon Portal](https://usmc.hackathon-portal.maximus.com).
- Coordinate TAD funding and travel through your unit or organization.
- Prepare to Bring Your Own Device (BYOD), including a laptop, chargers, and any required adapters.
- Coordinate data sharing and sanitization of any datasets with Hackathon Points of Contact (POCs) prior to arrival (see Section 7).
- Join the designated Slack channel and monitor communications at [MCU-NPS AI Hackathon Collaboration Workspace](URL is TBD).
- Attend the optional pre-event *Ask Me Anything (AMA)* session (details will be distributed via email).

---

## Data & Security Requirements

All Hackathon activity will be conducted at the **UNCLASSIFIED** level. **No classified systems, networks, or data are authorized.**

- Participants are encouraged to bring their own data but must coordinate with Hackathon POCs in advance.
- Controlled data must be appropriately sanitized, anonymized, and cleared for use **prior** to the hackathon.
- Only MCU and NPS appointed data stewards may clear data for use. A written letter or memorandum from the approving authority attesting that the data is cleared for use is required for inclusion in the hackathon.
- Any datasets that have not been cleared in advance are **not guaranteed** to be included in the Hackathon Portal.
- Open-source datasets are permitted. Participants are encouraged to explore repositories such as **GitHub**, **HuggingFace**, and **Kaggle** for open-source training and education datasets.

---

## Execution Expectations During the Event

Participants should be prepared for active engagement throughout the event.

- Arrive prepared to engage immediately on **15 September 2026 at 0900**.
- Following the welcome brief and technical briefs teams will complete formation on Day 1 and development will begin immediately.
- Final team presentations must clearly articulate **operational relevance and impact**.

---

## Logistics & Equipment

- Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) is **strongly encouraged**.
- Snacks and beverages will be provided.
- **Location:** Marine Corps University and Naval Postgraduate School
  **MCU Rooms:** Warner Auditorium and Lecture Hall #3
  **NPS Rooms:** Dudley Knox Library - Room 117
